Where is Charleston, West Virginia, and how is the city laid out?

Charleston is the state capital and its largest city, set on the Kanawha River where the Elk River joins it. It is the seat of Kanawha County, and its elevation runs from 597 to 1,167 feet. The city covers 32.5 square miles, of which 31.4 are land.

Fifteen named neighborhoods sit inside the city limits, from the East End and Edgewood historic districts to the West Side, South Hills, Kanawha City, Elk City, Fort Hill, Forest Hills and North Charleston. Others include Charleston Heights, Louden Heights, Riverview, Shadowlawn, South Park and South Ruffner. Flood exposure and house age vary by neighborhood, so name the neighborhood when you ask the city about an address.

Charleston factFigure
Population, July 1, 2025 estimate46,117 (Census Bureau)
Population, 202048,864
Highest count85,796 in 1960
Elevation range597 to 1,167 feet

CountyKanawha

How did Charleston's history shape its housing?

Settlers built Fort Lee by the Kanawha in April 1788, and Virginia designated 40 acres of George Clendenin's land as a town in December 1794. Salt was the first big industry, with the first furnace built in 1797, and salt works eventually lined the south bank in what is now Kanawha City.

The capital moved to Charleston in 1870, went back to Wheeling in 1875 and returned permanently in 1885. The Chesapeake and Ohio arrived in 1873, and between 1880 and 1930 the population rose from 4,192 to 60,408. A fire destroyed the Victorian capitol in January 1921, and the present building, designed by Cass Gilbert, was dedicated in 1932.

Urban renewal in the 1960s demolished many buildings, especially in the Triangle District. The encyclopedia says that after the demolition it took years for those areas to recover and that a number of vacant lots from that period still exist. Since the 1960 peak the city has lost population, which the encyclopedia ties to declining chemical industry jobs and out-migration.

What does the Charleston economy run on?

Government and health care anchor it, and the chemical industry is far smaller than it was. The Charleston Area Medical Center, created in 1972 by merging the major hospitals, serves southern West Virginia and is among the state's largest employers.

  • State government is based at the Capitol complex, and the Culture Center there houses the state archives and museum.
  • The Charleston area is home to Appalachian Power, United Bank and Gestamp, according to Wikipedia's list of companies headquartered there.
  • The University of Charleston, founded as Morris Harvey College, has about 1,000 students, and a West Virginia University branch campus serves as a clinical campus.
  • The Clay Center for the Arts and Sciences, the Vandalia Health Center civic center and the FestivALL events bring visitors.

The city's Municipal Auditorium, a 1939 art moderne landmark, closed in 2024 over structural and safety concerns.

What are Charleston's climate and flood risks?

Charleston has a humid subtropical climate with four seasons, and flooding is the hazard that most affects a house sale. The January daily average is 34.4 degrees Fahrenheit, the city sees about 23 days a year at 90 or above, and precipitation averages about 3.5 inches a month. Thunderstorms are frequent in late spring and summer and are occasionally severe.

The city's own floodplain page says Charleston has had 13 floods greater than the 1 percent annual chance flood, the last in 1934, and that damage has occurred in smaller events too. The Floodplain Manager reviews building permits and will determine whether a property is in a Special Flood Hazard Area, where flood insurance is typically required. An Elevation Certificate from a licensed surveyor or engineer can help set premiums and can support a map amendment request.

Charleston floodplain factDetail
Floods above the 1% annual chance flood13, the last in 1934
Community Rating System classClass 9, a 5% premium discount

Charleston is the only municipality in West Virginia in the Community Rating System. See the city floodplain management page and the state's flood hazard tool for any address.

How do roads, transit and schools affect a Charleston sale?

Charleston is crossed by Interstates 64, 77 and 79, and the West Virginia Turnpike ends at the city's southeastern edge. U.S. 60 and U.S. 119 run through the center, and West Virginia routes 25, 61, 62 and 114 lie within the limits. Yeager Airport is about two miles north of the interstates on route 114, and Amtrak's Cardinal stops in the city. The Kanawha Valley Regional Transportation Authority runs the buses.

Public schools belong to Kanawha County Schools. The city's high schools are Capital High School, George Washington High School in South Hills and the private Charleston Catholic High School. Confirm the school assignment for a specific address with the district.

What permits and repairs matter before selling a Charleston house?

All construction work in Charleston needs a permit before it begins, and the Building Department says homeowners may do their own work if permits are pulled and an inspection confirms the work meets code. The department issues permits for roofs, replacement windows, siding, fences, retaining walls, driveways, plumbing, electrical and HVAC, among other work.

  • Permit fees are waived for construction with a total job cost up to $2,500.
  • Contractors who start without a permit face a minimum $100 fee or twice the normal fee, whichever is greater, and a license suspension of at least three months.
  • Demolition permits require an asbestos report and details on capping the storm and sewer laterals.
  • Applications go to the Permit Coordinator, Building Department, 915 Quarrier Street, Suite 5, and the permit office number is 304-348-6833.

The permit rules apply to repairs made before a sale, and a buyer's inspection can raise questions about unpermitted work.

Who collects and who assesses property tax on a Charleston home?

Kanawha County, not the city, bills property tax. The Kanawha County Sheriff's Tax Division collects it, and the Kanawha County Assessor values the property.

OfficeDetailsPhone
Kanawha County Sheriff's Tax Office409 Virginia Street East, Room 120, Charleston, WV 25301; Charleston hours Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 5:00304-357-0210
Kanawha County Assessor (Sallie Robinson)Kanawha County Courthouse, 409 Virginia Street East304-357-0250

The tax office also runs detachments in Cross Lanes, Sissonville, Elkview, Jefferson and Quincy, and its page says it mails roughly 100,000 real estate tickets and 95,000 personal property tickets each July. The statewide calendar applies: tickets on or after July 15, installments due September 1 and March 1, a 2.5 percent discount before each date, delinquency on October 1 and April 1, and 9 percent annual interest on late tax. Property inside a municipality that is not an owner-occupied home is Class IV, which the state taxes at four times the Class I rate, while owner-occupied residential property is Class II at two times.

What do closing costs look like on a Charleston sale?

The main government charge is the transfer tax recorded with the deed. West Virginia Code 11-22-2 sets $1.10 per $500 of value, kept by the county since July 1, 2025, plus an additional county tax of 55 cents per $500 unless the commission has raised it, plus a $20 fee on transfers for consideration.

On a $150,000 deed at those base rates the amounts are $330, $165 and $20, a total of $515. The grantor pays unless the grantee accepts the deed with the tax unpaid. Unpaid property tax, prior mortgages and any liens come out of the proceeds, so ask the sheriff's office for the tax status before you accept any number.

What do Charleston sellers usually face?

Three situations are worth planning for: older houses, properties near the rivers and inherited homes. The East End and Edgewood carry historic district designations, and homes near the Kanawha and Elk rivers raise the flood questions covered above.

A list, a sale by owner or a cash sale each handles those issues differently. A listing brings showings and buyer financing, and a cash sale usually involves a title search, payoff of any liens, and a deed recorded with the county. Compare what each leaves you after taxes, liens and transfer costs, not the headline price alone.

More questions about Charleston, WV

Does the City of Charleston or Kanawha County collect property tax?

Kanawha County does. The Sheriff's Tax Division at 409 Virginia Street East collects it, and the phone number is 304-357-0210.

Do I need a permit for a roof or window replacement in Charleston?

Yes. The city's Building Department lists roofs and replacement windows among the work that needs a permit, and fees are waived only when the total job cost is $2,500 or less.

How do I find out if a Charleston house is in a flood zone?

Ask the city's Floodplain Manager for a floodplain determination, or check the state's flood hazard tool. A property in a Special Flood Hazard Area typically needs flood insurance, and an Elevation Certificate can help with premiums.

What transfer tax applies when I sell a Charleston house?

The base rates are $1.10 per $500 of value plus an additional county tax of 55 cents per $500, plus a $20 fee, unless the Kanawha County Commission has raised its rate. The seller pays unless the buyer accepts the deed with the tax unpaid.

When are Kanawha County property taxes due?

Installments are due September 1 and March 1, with a 2.5 percent discount for paying before each date. Unpaid halves become delinquent on October 1 and April 1 and accrue 9 percent interest.

Where is Huntington, WV, and how is the city laid out?

Huntington sits on the southern bank of the Ohio River where the Guyandotte River joins it, in the southwestern corner of West Virginia. It is the county seat of Cabell County, and small parts of the city extend into Wayne County. Wikipedia reports a 2020 census population of 46,842, an estimate of 44,942 for 2024, and a ranking as the second-largest city in the state.

The city covers about 18.5 square miles, of which roughly 16.2 are land, and sits at 564 feet above sea level. Streets follow a grid. Avenues run east and west alongside the river, with Third and Fifth Avenues as the wide boulevards, and numbered streets run north and south.

Locals divide the city into four sections. The CSX railroad tracks split north from south, and First Street splits east from west. Within those sections you find:

  • Downtown and the Marshall University campus
  • West Huntington, Old Central City and Westmoreland on the west side
  • Ritter Park, South Side, Enslow Park and the Southeast Hills to the south
  • Walnut Hills, Guyandotte, Highlawn and Forest Hills on the east side

Knowing which section your house sits in helps when you talk to any buyer.

What shaped Huntington's economy and housing stock?

Huntington grew as a rail, river and steel town, and the housing stock still reflects that. According to Wikipedia, the city was founded in 1871 by Collis P. Huntington, and its boom years ran until the Great Flood of 1937.

Population peaked decades ago and has fallen in every census since 1950. The city went from 86,353 residents in 1950 to 46,842 in 2020.

The job base has shifted toward health care and education. Wikipedia lists the largest employers as Marshall University, Cabell Huntington Hospital, St. Mary's Medical Center, Amazon, DirecTV and the City of Huntington. St. Mary's alone is described as the largest private employer in Cabell County, with more than 2,600 employees.

Jobs like these bring relocations in and out, and some of those owners need a quick closing.

How do floods and weather affect a Huntington house sale?

The Ohio River is the reason Huntington has flood walls, and flood history is part of the city's story. The Great Flood of 1937 killed five people, left tens of thousands homeless and led to the construction of the flood walls in 1938, according to Wikipedia. Buyers and lenders still ask about flood zone status, so check your address on the state's flood map tool before you list.

The climate is humid subtropical at the northern edge of its range. Snowfall averages about 19.8 inches a season, and a typical year brings 24 afternoons at or above 90 degrees.

ItemFigureWhy a seller cares

Afternoons below freezingAbout 16 to 17 a yearPipe and heating checks
Flood walls built1938Flood zone questions at inspection

None of this makes a house unsellable, but roof, basement and heating condition are what any buyer will price in.

What local rules does a Huntington seller or landlord need to know?

The biggest local rule for owners with tenants is the rental registry and inspection program. Huntington City Council adopted an ordinance in 2018 requiring rental units to meet building, fire, health, safety and zoning codes. The city's rental inspection page explains how it works.

The city cites a 2020 housing report that found 6,050 of its 9,603 rental units, or 63 percent, in decline, and estimated that 60 to 80 percent did not meet code.

  • One and two family rentals are inspected no more than once in 12 months per unit.
  • Inspections cover electrical safety, heating, smoke alarms, handrails and general maintenance.
  • Tenants can request an inspection without the landlord's permission.
  • Apartment buildings with more than two units go through the building, electrical and plumbing inspectors and the fire marshal.

If you own a rental you want to sell, an open violation or an unregistered unit can slow a conventional buyer's lender. A buyer paying cash can often take the property with those issues still open. For code complaints on vacant or neglected property, the city directory lists the Public Works office at 304-696-4414.

The 2023 registry packet listed a $75 inspection fee and a $20 business license, so confirm current fees with the city before relying on those figures.

How does property tax work for a house in Huntington?

Huntington homes are taxed by Cabell County, with the Cabell County Assessor valuing the property and the Sheriff's Tax Office collecting the bill. The assessor's FAQ page lists the 2026 levy rates for owner occupied homes as 1.6752 inside the City of Huntington and 1.3552 in the rural part of the county. Residents of the cities of Barboursville and Milton pay their own city rates.

West Virginia sorts property into classes. Class 2 is owner occupied residential property, and Classes 3 and 4 cover non owner occupied property. A house that stops being your primary residence, for example after you move out and rent it or leave it empty, is assessed differently, which is a common surprise for heirs.

Under the state due dates, bills go out on or after July 15, the first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1. A 2.5 percent discount applies if you pay before those dates. Unpaid first half taxes become delinquent October 1 and second half taxes April 1, and delinquent taxes accrue interest at 9 percent a year.

In Cabell County, owners aged 65 or older who have lived in West Virginia for two consecutive years can apply for the homestead exemption between July 1 and December 1. The state describes the benefit as an exemption of the first $20,000 of assessed value.

What does it cost to transfer a house in West Virginia?

West Virginia charges an excise tax on the privilege of transferring real estate, and it is the main closing tax on a deed. Under section 11-22-2 of the state code the rate is $1.10 for each $500 of value, and the county collects it. A second county excise tax of 55 cents per $500 also applies, and a county commission may raise that to a maximum of $1.65 per $500 by vote.

The grantor, meaning the seller, pays unless the buyer accepts the deed without the tax being paid. The clerk also collects a $20 fee that goes to the state Affordable Housing Fund when real estate is transferred for consideration.

Sale price$1.10 per $500Add 55 cents per $500
$60,000$132$198
$100,000$220$330

These examples are arithmetic from the statute rates, not a quote, and your county's actual combined rate may differ. Deeds in Cabell County are recorded with the County Clerk, whose records include a deed lookup. Transfers by will or through a list of heirs are excluded from the tax under section 11-22-1, which matters for inherited homes.

Which Huntington sellers usually consider a cash sale?

Sellers in Huntington who consider a cash sale usually face one of a few situations, and each one has a local twist. The common thread is a house that would take time and money to prepare for a conventional listing.

  • Heirs holding an older home in Old Central City, Guyandotte or the South Side that no one wants to maintain.
  • Landlords with units that fail the city's rental inspection and need work they cannot fund.
  • Owners relocating for a job at one of the hospitals or Marshall University on a short timeline.
  • Homes with a damp basement, an aging roof or an outdated furnace that would draw repair demands from a buyer's inspector.

A cash offer skips the lender's appraisal and the repair negotiation after inspection. Cash Home Buyers reviews each Huntington property individually, and an offer depends on the condition, location and the work the house needs. If the numbers do not suit you, you can say no and owe nothing.

Before you accept any offer, ask for the closing to be handled by a West Virginia title company or attorney, confirm who pays the transfer tax, and get the payoff on any mortgage or tax lien in writing.

How do Huntington's roads and transit affect where a house sells?

Interstate 64 and US 60 shape how buyers think about Huntington. Exits 6 through 15 of I-64 serve the city, and US 52 connects at exit 6. US 60, part of the historic Midland Trail, runs along the river through downtown and splits into Third and Fifth Avenues.

The Huntington and Ashland metro area spans seven counties in three states, with an estimated 368,000 residents, so buyers and renters often come from across the river.

The assessor's page also links to the Tri-State Transit Authority and the Greater Huntington Park and Recreation District, handy references when you describe the area to an out of town buyer.

More questions about Huntington, WV

How fast can I sell my house in Huntington, WV?

A cash sale can close faster than a conventional sale because there is no lender appraisal. The exact timing depends on title work and the Cabell County Clerk's recording process. Ask for a closing date in writing before you sign.

Do I pay a transfer tax when I sell in Huntington?

Yes, in most sales. West Virginia charges $1.10 per $500 of value, plus a county excise tax that starts at 55 cents per $500, and the seller normally pays. Inherited transfers by will or list of heirs are excluded under section 11-22-1.

What happens to my Huntington rental if it fails an inspection?

The city requires a landlord to correct violations found at a registered rental inspection. If you sell instead, a cash buyer can take the property as is, but disclose known problems and confirm the sale with your title company.

When are Cabell County property taxes due?

The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1. First half taxes become delinquent October 1, and second half taxes April 1. A 2.5 percent discount applies when you pay early.

Can I sell a house in Huntington that I inherited?

Yes, once you have legal authority to convey the title. That usually means the estate has been opened with the county. A title company can tell you which documents the deed needs.

What is Morgantown, WV, and where does it sit?

Morgantown is the county seat of Monongalia County and lies along the Monongahela River, close to the Pennsylvania border. Wikipedia gives its 2020 census population as 30,347 and an estimate of 30,490 for 2024, which makes it the third-largest city in West Virginia. The wider metro area is estimated at about 140,000 people.

The city is small on the map, at 10.62 square miles, and it is about 75 miles south of Pittsburgh. Charleston is roughly 156 miles to the southwest.

Several neighborhoods began as separate towns and were annexed as Morgantown grew, and some are partly or fully outside the city limits even though everyone calls them Morgantown. The list includes:

  • First Ward, Second Ward and South Park near downtown
  • Sunnyside and Wiles Hill beside the downtown university campus
  • Evansdale, Greenmont and Woodburn
  • Suncrest, South Hills and North Hills
  • Sabraton, the Mileground and Easton, which are in part or entirely outside the city

That last point matters for sellers, because a house with a Morgantown address may sit outside the city limits.

How does West Virginia University shape the Morgantown housing market?

West Virginia University is the center of the local economy, and it shapes who buys and rents houses. WVU is the state's flagship public university. Wikipedia reports enrollment above 25,000 in 2024 and says the city hosts about 30,000 students, roughly the same as its permanent population.

Wikipedia describes Sunnyside, just north of downtown, as an older neighborhood that has long been known for student housing. A house in or near that area is often valued as a rental, not a family home, so the buyer pool leans toward investors.

The health system adds to the job base. According to WVU Government Relations, WVU Medicine supported 56,224 jobs statewide in fiscal year 2024. Another source, the Morgantown airport's economic baseline study, reported that WVU employed 6,500 people in 2011 and called it the largest single employer in the area. That figure is old, so treat it as a sense of scale.

If your house is a student rental with a lease running, tell any buyer the lease dates up front, since they affect when a buyer can take possession.

What does a Morgantown landlord need to know before selling?

Every rental unit inside the city is registered and inspected on a regular cycle. The city's rental information page says registered rentals are inspected once every three years under the International Property Maintenance Code, and owners must correct any violations found.

The city's code enforcement page explains the history. From 1979 until 1989 Morgantown followed housing codes written by city officials and approved by City Council. In 1989 the State of West Virginia adopted its first official written housing code.

TopicWhat the city says
Who must registerRental housing inside city limits
Inspection cycleOnce every 3 years

If you plan to sell a student rental, pull your registration and your last inspection result first. An open violation does not stop a sale, but it gives a conventional buyer a reason to negotiate. An investor paying cash can usually take on the repair list, so the price is the main question.

How do Morgantown's roads, transit and airport affect a sale?

Morgantown is served by I-79, I-68, US 19, US 119, WV 7 and WV 705. Buyers who commute pay attention to which of these a house is near.

Morgantown also has two systems you will not find elsewhere in the state. The Mountain Line Transit Authority runs most of the bus service, and its Grey Line operates every day of the year between Clarksburg and Pittsburgh International Airport. The Morgantown Personal Rapid Transit system has five stations and covers 8.65 miles. Its stations are Walnut, Beechurst, Engineering, Towers and Medical.

  • Morgantown Municipal Airport sits about 3 miles northeast of downtown on US 119.
  • North Central West Virginia Airport is about 35 miles away by road.
  • Pittsburgh International is about 80 miles away.

Describe your house's access to these routes accurately and let the buyer judge.

What is the climate like, and how does it affect a Morgantown house?

Morgantown has four distinct seasons at the boundary of humid subtropical and humid continental climates. The January daily mean is 32.0 degrees, and average annual snowfall is 27.6 inches. Summers are hot and humid, with a July mean of 74.1 degrees and about 13.2 days a year at or above 90.

Precipitation is generous. May through July is the wettest period, according to Wikipedia's summary of 1991 to 2020 airport normals. For a house, that means gutters, grading and basement moisture are routine inspection topics, and a recent roof or drainage repair helps a listing.

Whatever the house's age, a recent roof or drainage repair is worth mentioning to any buyer.

How do property taxes work for a Morgantown house?

The Monongalia County Assessor values the property and the County Sheriff's Tax Office collects the tax. The assessor's page for new residents states that real and personal property are assessed to the owner of record on July 1. If you sell after that date, the tax year still reflects you as owner, so plan for how the current bill will be handled at closing.

The Sheriff's Tax Office mails statements in July and sells delinquent real estate taxes in November, according to its website. State rules set the payment calendar:

  • Bills are issued on or after July 15.
  • The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1.
  • Paying before those dates earns a 2.5 percent discount.
  • Delinquent taxes accrue interest at 9 percent a year, per the West Virginia Tax Division.

For questions about paying real estate taxes, the assessor's website directs residents to the Sheriff's tax department at 304-291-7244. A tax lien that goes unpaid can complicate a sale, so confirm the status with the title company early.

What does selling a Morgantown house cost at closing?

The main government charge is the West Virginia transfer excise tax. Under section 11-22-2, the rate is $1.10 for each $500 of value, plus an additional county excise tax of 55 cents per $500 that a county commission may raise. The seller, as grantor, normally pays, and a $20 fee also goes to the state's Affordable Housing Fund.

At a base combined rate of $1.65 per $500, a $200,000 sale works out to $660. That is arithmetic from the statute, not a quote, and your county's current rate and the deed's stated value control. A will or an intestate list of heirs is excluded from the tax under section 11-22-1.

A traditional sale adds agent commissions, repairs requested after inspection and carrying costs while the house is listed. A cash sale to Cash Home Buyers is aimed at skipping those steps, and an offer depends on the property. If it does not work for you, you owe nothing.

More questions about Morgantown, WV

Can I sell a rental house in Morgantown with open code violations?

Yes. The city requires owners to correct violations found at inspection, but an investor paying cash may buy the property as is. Check the registration and your latest inspection result first so the title company has the facts.

Who collects property tax in Monongalia County?

The Monongalia County Sheriff's Tax Office collects real estate and personal property taxes. The Assessor values the property. Statements are mailed in July, and delinquent real estate taxes are sold in November.

Is a house outside the Morgantown city limits treated differently?

Possibly. Areas such as the Mileground, Easton and parts of Sabraton are in part or entirely outside city limits, so ask the city and county offices which rules cover your address.

Do I owe transfer tax if I inherited my Morgantown house and sell it?

The tax applies to the deed when you sell. Transfers by will or through a list of heirs are excluded, so receiving the house from the estate is not taxed that way, but your sale deed to the buyer generally is.

How quickly can a cash sale close in Morgantown?

It depends on title work and recording, not on a lender. Ask for a target closing date in writing and confirm the title company that will handle the deed.

Where is Parkersburg, WV, and how did it grow?

Parkersburg is the seat of Wood County and sits where the Little Kanawha River meets the Ohio River. Wikipedia lists the 2020 census population at 29,738, which ranks it fourth in the state, and the Parkersburg and Vienna metro area at 89,490.

Settlers first called the town Newport. Land had been granted to Alexander Parker for Revolutionary War service, a title dispute with the town planners was settled in 1809 in favor of his heirs, and the town took the name Parkersburg in 1810. It was chartered in 1820 and rechartered as a city in 1860.

The Baltimore and Ohio Railroad built a branch line south from Wheeling in 1857 and a railroad bridge to Belpre, Ohio between 1868 and 1870. The city covers about 12.35 square miles, of which 11.82 are land.

The Little Kanawha divides the city into a north side and a south side. South Parkersburg was a separate city until it joined Parkersburg in 1950.

Which Parkersburg neighborhoods do sellers hear about most?

The north end holds most of the named neighborhoods, and each has a different housing style. Wikipedia lists these areas on the north side:

  • Downtown, Julia-Ann Square and Quincy Hill
  • Beechwood, Fairview Heights and Granada Hills
  • Meadowcrest, Oakwood Estates and Woodland Park
  • Riverside, Worthington and the East End

South of the river, the former city of South Parkersburg is joined by suburban areas of southern Wood County, including Blennerhassett, Lubeck and Washington to the southwest and Mineral Wells to the southeast. Some of those sit outside the city, so tax and code rules differ by address.

Which part of town your house falls into can affect flood zone status, which the next section covers.

What is the Parkersburg floodwall, and does it affect my house?

The Parkersburg Floodwall protects low lying parts of the city along the Ohio and Little Kanawha rivers, and owners inside the protected zone pay a maintenance fee. The city code, in Article 783, defines the protected flood zone as all properties at or below an average of 624 feet above sea level that the floodwall protects. The City Engineer determines the boundaries. You can read the definitions in the city's codified ordinances.

The code declares that owners of property in the flood zone are the users and beneficiaries of the floodwall and bear the cost of its continuance, maintenance and improvement. Article 783 also sets a payment schedule and penalties and is administered by the city's Director of Finance. A Parkersburg Flood Wall Board is established separately in the administrative code.

ItemWhat the city code says
Protected flood zoneProperties at or below about 624 feet above sea level, protected by the floodwall
Who sets the boundaryThe City Engineer
Who pays maintenance feesOwners of property in the zone
Who administers itDirector of Finance
Residential buildingDefined to exclude rentals of four or more units on one tract

If you are selling inside that zone, find out whether any floodwall fees are unpaid, because the code includes penalties. A title company can also confirm whether a balance affects the closing. Anyone can check a specific address on the state's flood map tool.

How does code enforcement work for a vacant or neglected house in Parkersburg?

The city's Code Enforcement Division is the enforcement arm for building, health and safety, zoning and nuisance codes. Its stated goal is voluntary compliance from property and business owners, and it takes further steps where that fails. The division's page describes this approach.

A separate body, the Building Enforcement Agency, meets monthly. The city's boards page says it meets on the first Monday of each month at 9:00 a.m. and includes the Mayor, the City Engineer and the Code Enforcement Director. The city says the agency works to address neglected, vacant and abandoned properties, which it describes as critical to the stability of residents, small businesses and the community.

State law supports this work. West Virginia Code section 8-12-16c gives a municipality authority to create a vacant building and property registration and maintenance program by ordinance.

  • Keep grass and exterior debris under control while a house sits empty.
  • Respond to any notice from the division in writing and keep a copy.
  • Ask the division about open complaints before you sign a sale contract.

An owner who inherits a neglected house and cannot afford repairs may find a direct sale simpler than going through a repair schedule. Cash Home Buyers looks at each Parkersburg property as is, with no obligation if you decline an offer.

What drives the Parkersburg economy and who buys homes here?

Parkersburg's economy mixes chemicals, finance and federal government work. The city's economy page names DuPont, Highmark, United Bank and Woodcraft among the well known companies, and says the U.S. Treasury's Bureau of the Fiscal Service employs more than 2,000 local people.

Population has declined in each census since 1960, when it was 44,797, falling to 29,738 in 2020. The city had 13,119 households and 15,246 housing units in 2020 according to Wikipedia's census summary, about 2,100 more housing units than households.

Education adds demand. West Virginia University at Parkersburg is a public college on the outskirts of the city, and the city has three high schools: Parkersburg High, Parkersburg South and Parkersburg Catholic. Public schools are run by Wood County Schools, which also operates the Wood County Technical Center and the Caperton Center for Applied Technology.

Chemical plant, bank, federal and college jobs bring people in and out of the area, and that turnover is part of why homes change hands here.

How do taxes work for a Parkersburg property?

Wood County assesses and taxes Parkersburg property, and real estate taxes are paid at the Wood County Sheriff's office, not the Assessor. The Wood County Assessor's page says property is assessed July 1 and that your tax bill multiplies a levy rate by your assessed value, which is 60 percent of market value. Levy rates are set by the legislature for the Board of Education, the county commission and the municipalities.

The assessor's FAQ flags two points that surprise owners:

  • A home deeded to an LLC cannot be taxed as Class 2 residential property, so all LLC owned property is taxed as Class 3 or 4.
  • Only an owner occupied home with the owner's name on the deed can have Class 2 status, so a relative living in another home you own does not qualify.

State dates apply: bills issue on or after July 15, the first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1, with a 2.5 percent discount for early payment and 9 percent annual interest on delinquent amounts. See the Tax Division page.

When you sell, the transfer excise tax under section 11-22-2 is $1.10 per $500 of value, plus a county excise tax of 55 cents per $500 that counties can raise. The seller normally pays it, and a $20 fee goes to the state Affordable Housing Fund.

How do roads, rail and the airport connect Parkersburg?

Interstate 77 and US 50 are the two major highways, and WV routes 2, 14, 47, 68, 95 and 618 also pass through the city. The Mid-Ohio Valley Regional Airport had three flights a day on weekdays from Charlotte, per Wikipedia. Passenger trains stopped in the 1960s, with Amtrak's Shenandoah running from 1976 to 1981, and CSX still provides freight service.

These links matter to out of town heirs, who often need to handle a sale from a distance. A remote closing with a title company can be arranged if you cannot travel.

More questions about Parkersburg, WV

Does the Parkersburg floodwall fee affect my sale?

It can if your property is inside the protected flood zone. Article 783 of the city code assigns the maintenance cost to those owners and sets penalties. Ask the city's finance office whether anything is unpaid before closing.

Who do I call about code problems on a vacant Parkersburg house?

The city's Building and Code Enforcement department handles building, health and safety, zoning and nuisance codes. Contact it before you sell so any open notice is known.

Why is my Parkersburg house taxed as non-residential?

West Virginia allows Class 2 residential status only for an owner occupied home with the owner's name on the deed. A house deeded to an LLC is taxed as Class 3 or 4, according to the Wood County Assessor.

When are Wood County property taxes due?

The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1, with delinquency starting October 1 and April 1. Pay the Wood County Sheriff, not the Assessor.

Can I sell a Parkersburg house if I live out of state?

Yes. Title companies can handle signing by mail or remote notary. Confirm who is arranging the closing and how the deed will be recorded.

Wheeling at a glance

Selling in Wheeling?

Where is Wheeling, WV, and why is its housing stock so old?

Wheeling is the seat of Ohio County and the largest city in West Virginia's Northern Panhandle, lying along the Ohio River about 11 miles west of Pennsylvania. Wikipedia gives a 2020 population of 27,062, fifth in the state, and a metro population of 139,513. Parts of the city lie in Marshall County.

The city grew early. It was the endpoint of the National Road, and the Wheeling Suspension Bridge, completed in 1849, linked downtown with Wheeling Island. The Baltimore and Ohio Railroad arrived in 1853. Wheeling hosted the conventions that led to West Virginia's separation from Virginia, and it served as the state capital from 1861 to 1870 and again from 1875 to 1885.

Population peaked at 61,659 in the 1930 census and has fallen since heavy industry declined. Wikipedia notes that prosperous residents built fine houses, especially on Wheeling Island, during the growth years. Housing from those decades remains, so ask for a full condition review of any older Wheeling house.

The city covers 16.01 square miles, of which 13.79 are land, and Wheeling Creek runs through it to meet the Ohio River downtown.

Which Wheeling neighborhoods are most distinct?

Wheeling has dozens of named neighborhoods, and the hillsides and the island create very different settings. The list on Wikipedia includes several that sellers often mention:

  • Wheeling Island, in the middle of the Ohio River
  • North Wheeling, East Wheeling, South Wheeling and Center Wheeling
  • Warwood, Woodsdale, Oakmont and Pleasant Valley
  • Oglebay Park, Park View and Wheeling Heights
  • Arbordale, Pleasanton, Springdale and Dimmeydale

Some neighborhoods, such as Benwood, Mozart, Mount Olivet and Sherrard, are partly or mostly in Marshall County, so an address that says Wheeling may be billed by a different county. Always confirm the county before you look up taxes.

The city also has a North Wheeling Design Review process and a Historic Landmarks Commission. If your house is in a historic area, ask the Building and Planning department whether exterior changes need review before you commit to repairs.

What flood risk should a Wheeling seller expect?

Flood zones in Wheeling are common. The city's Building and Planning FAQ says property along the Ohio River, Wheeling Creek and its larger tributaries is in the flood zone, and that every ward in the city contains flood zones. To check a specific property, enter the address in the state's flood map tool.

The city's Building Code Official also serves as floodplain manager, and the department lists NFIP floodplain development guidelines on its building code services page. Fences in the floodplain need a building permit, which is a detail owners often miss.

QuestionCity answer
Where are flood zones?Along the Ohio River, Wheeling Creek and larger tributaries
Which wards have them?Every ward
Who manages the floodplain?The Building Code Official, as floodplain manager
Is a permit needed for a fence?Yes, for fences in the floodplain

For a seller, the practical step is to find out your flood zone status before you accept an offer, since lenders and insurers use it. Annual precipitation in Wheeling averages about 41.88 inches, spread evenly through the year, per Wikipedia.

What are Wheeling's vacant building and demolition rules?

Wheeling requires owners of vacant structures to register them, and neglected buildings can be ordered repaired or razed. The Vacant Structure Code, adopted by City Council in 2009, tracks ownership and encourages maintenance. Once a building is registered, the owner has a year to renovate and occupy it, tear it down or sell it before a fee is assessed, and fees increase for each year the building stays vacant.

The Building Code Services page explains the enforcement side. Owners must either maintain or raze their buildings. Irresponsible owners may receive a Raze or Repair Order, and failure to comply can mean a Municipal Court appearance and a monetary penalty. Where public health and safety are at risk, the city may raze the structure and place a lien on the property for the cost, without taking ownership.

  • A vacant registered building gets one year before fees start.
  • Fees rise each year the building stays vacant.
  • A city demolition becomes a lien against the property.

The sale option matters here. The program says an owner can sell within the first year without a fee, so a prompt sale can stop the clock. If you inherited a vacant Wheeling house, that is worth knowing early. Cash Home Buyers reviews houses as is, including ones that need major work, and you owe nothing if you decline.

What permits and codes apply to repairs on a Wheeling house?

The city uses the 2018 International Building and Residential Codes and the 2018 International Property Maintenance Code, with the 2020 National Electric Code. A building permit costs $4.00 per $1,000 of job cost, rounded up to the next $1,000, so a $5,600 project costs $24.00. A new electric service adds a $25 residential fee.

Most applications are reviewed within 48 hours, and larger projects can take up to a week. Roofing, siding and window permits can sometimes be issued the same day. Permits are required for work that sellers commonly consider before listing:

  • A new roof, siding or kitchen and bathroom renovation
  • Electrical upgrades and new decks
  • Garage or carport construction
  • Fences in the floodplain or over 7 feet
  • Retaining walls over 48 inches

Unpermitted work can surface in a buyer's inspection and slow a sale. The city also notes that it cannot use federal community development funds for home repairs on pre 1970 construction because of lead based paint rules, so there is no city repair grant to count on. A buyer who purchases as is avoids that repair path altogether.

How does property tax work for a Wheeling house?

Ohio County's Sheriff's Tax Office collects real estate and personal property taxes, and the County Assessor values the property. The tax office is at 1500 Chapline Street, Room 206, and the office page lists these deadlines:

  • September 1: first half discount ends
  • October 1: first half taxes become delinquent and interest begins
  • March 1: second half discount ends
  • April 1: second half taxes become delinquent
  • April 30: unpaid taxes are subject to publication and added fees
  • October 31: unpaid delinquent real estate taxes are certified to the state auditor

Statements are mailed in July. You can search records and pay online at wvpropertytaxes.com, where the office lists a $1.00 fee for electronic checks and $1.00 plus 2.2 percent for cards.

Statewide, assessed value is 60 percent of market value, according to the Wood County assessor's explanation of the same state system, and the first $20,000 of assessed value of an owner occupied home is exempt for owners 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled. See the Tax Division exemption list.

What will closing a Wheeling sale cost in transfer taxes?

The deed is taxed under West Virginia's transfer excise tax, which the seller normally pays. Under section 11-22-2, the rate is $1.10 for each $500 of value, plus a county excise tax of 55 cents per $500 that a county commission can raise, and a $20 fee for the Affordable Housing Fund.

On an $80,000 sale, the base $1.10 rate comes to $176, and adding the 55 cent county tax brings it to $264. That is arithmetic from the statute, not a quote. Deeds are recorded by the Ohio County Clerk.

Transfers by will or through a list of heirs are excluded under section 11-22-1.

How do roads and transit connect Wheeling?

I-70 and I-470 run through the city and link it with Pittsburgh's suburbs and Ohio, and US 40, US 250 and WV Route 2 also serve it. The Fort Henry Bridge carries I-70 across the river, and the interstate passes under Wheeling Hill through the Wheeling Tunnel. The county also runs the Wheeling Ohio County Airport.

The Robert C. Byrd Intermodal Transportation Center is the hub for Greyhound and for regional bus service run by the Ohio Valley Regional Transit Authority.

More questions about Wheeling, WV

What happens if my Wheeling house has been vacant for over a year?

Under the city's Vacant Structure Code, registered owners get a year before a fee is assessed, and fees rise each year the building stays vacant. Selling is one of the allowed ways to resolve it.

Is my Wheeling house in a flood zone?

The city says every ward contains flood zones, mostly along the Ohio River, Wheeling Creek and larger tributaries. Enter your address in the state flood map tool to check.

When are Ohio County property taxes due?

The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1. First half taxes become delinquent October 1, and second half taxes April 1.

What is a Raze or Repair Order?

It is a notice from the city's Building Inspection division requiring an owner to repair or demolish a building. Ignoring it can lead to Municipal Court and a lien for the city's demolition cost.

Who pays transfer tax on a Wheeling sale?

The seller normally pays it unless the buyer accepts the deed without it being paid. The state rate is $1.10 per $500, with a county tax starting at 55 cents per $500.
